stories.title: After Akhil Gogoi’s hunger strike, CPI(M) protests delayed Assam flood relief
stories.summary: Protestors scuffle with police personnel at various points during their thwarted march to Dispur, the State’s seat of power
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Less than a week after Raijor Dal president and MLA Akhil Gogoi began his indefinite hunger strike demanding immediate financial assistance to flood-affected families, members of the Communist Party of India (Marxist) organised a protest rally on Wednesday (October 7, 2026) to press for a similar demand.

According to Nirankush Nath, CPI(M) State Secretariat member, more than 2,000 protestors were detained following scuffles with police personnel at various points during their thwarted march to Dispur, the State’s seat of power.

The protestors demanded immediate relief and rehabilitation for the flood-affected people of eastern Assam, particularly in Charaideo and Sivasagar districts, and a judicial inquiry into the causes of the devastating floods in June.

The other demands included the formation of a North East Flood Management Authority, recognition of floods and erosion in Assam as a national problem, measures to halt the rising prices of essential commodities, and the immediate resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.

Mr. Nath said thousands of people from different parts of the State were scheduled to participate in the march, but the police and civil administration imposed a virtual ban on assembly and movement of protestors and heavily barricaded the entry points to Guwahati.
“Large numbers of protestors were intercepted at different locations, picked up by the police and taken to a designated protest ground for detention.
There were scuffles between protestors and police at several points,” he said.

Among those detained were senior leaders of the Assam State Committee, including State Secretary Suprakash Talukdar, Central Committee Member Isfaqur Rahman and veteran party leader Deben Bhattacharya.
Meanwhile, Mr. Gogoi’s hunger strike entered its sixth day on Wednesday.
His demands include ₹10 lakh compensation for each flood-hit family and a Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) probe into the eastern Assam floods.
Reacting to his fast, Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma said the financial assistance to flood-affected people was being delayed so that Mr. Gogoi could not claim credit for its release.
Mr. Gogoi represents the Sivasagar Assembly constituency, among the worst affected during the floods in June.

New Delhi: The Supreme Court on Wednesday agreed to examine an application seeking recall of its September 23 split verdict on the 2023 law governing the appointment of the Chief Election Commissioner and Election Commissioners.
The Supreme Court’s next step could determine the course of the challenge to the 2023 CEC appointments law.
The CJI may decide whether the recall application is maintainable and whether the September 23 split verdict should be reconsidered.
Depending on the court’s decision, the matter could either proceed on the basis of the existing split verdict or be placed before an appropriate larger bench for further consideration.
A separate curative petition filed by another party could also follow its own legal process.
Senior Advocate Gopal Sankaranarayanan mentioned the recall application before Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana.
The CJI said the court would examine the application before deciding whether to take it up.
The application seeks recall of the September 23 verdict delivered by a bench of Justices Dipankar Datta and Satish Chandra Sharma.
The two judges gave divergent views on whether challenges to the 2023 law should be referred to a larger Constitution Bench.
Justice Datta held that a larger-bench reference was not necessary, while Justice Sharma favoured such a reference.
The split meant that the issue had to be placed before the CJI for administrative consideration of the constitution of an appropriate bench.

stories.title: RP Act | Election Petition Must Be Presented Petitioner Himself & Not Counsel : Supreme Court

article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Wednesday (October 7) has held that an election petition filed under the Representation of the People Act, 1951 (RP Act) must be presented by the election petitioner himself, and that non-compliance with this mandatory requirement renders the petition liable to be dismissed.

A Bench of Justice Prashant Kumar Mishra and Justice Shree Chandrashekhar upheld the Madras High Court's dismissal of an election petition challenging the election of DMK MLA S. Regupathy from the Thirumayam Assembly Constituency in the 2026 Tamil Nadu Assembly elections, after noting that the Election Petition was not filed by the election petitioner, but by his counsel.

“…an election petition is a serious proceeding which may result in the vitiation of an electoral process and that the procedure prescribed by an election statute must, therefore, be strictly followed.

The requirement that the petition be presented “by” the petitioner enables the High Court, at the stage of presentation itself, to undertake a preliminary verification so as to ensure that the proceeding is not frivolous or vexatious.”, the Court observed, relying on its 2009 judgment of G.V. Sreerama Reddy and Another.
Returning Officer and Others.
The petitioner, V. Pon.

Paneerselvam, who was a candidate on the Thirumayam seat, had challenged the election on allegations including corrupt practice of undue influence arising from alleged suppression and false declaration of his spouse's assets and income in the statutory Form 26 affidavit.
The Madras High Court dismissed the election petition, after finding that it had been presented by the petitioner's counsel rather than by the petitioner personally.
The petitioner approached the Supreme Court against the dismissal.

Refusing to interfere with the impugned findings, the judgment authored by Justice Mishra examined Sections 81 and 86 of the RP Act, which respectively prescribe the requirements for presentation of an election petition and the consequence of non-compliance.
Relying on its earlier decision in G.V. Sreerama Reddy.

Returning Officer, the Court noted that Section 81(1) contains five specific requirements: the petitioner must be a candidate or elector; the petition must be presented “by” the petitioner; it must be based on specified statutory grounds; it must be presented before the High Court; and it must be filed within the prescribed 45-day period.

stories.headline: Houthis claim new attacks on Saudi Arabia, Yemen's Aden airport
stories.title: Houthis claim new attacks on Saudi Arabia, Yemen's Aden airport
stories.summary: Cairo, Oct 07: Iran-backed Houthi rebels in Yemen on Wednesday claimed attacks on military facilities and airports in neighbouring Saudi Arabia as the escalation deepened the latest front in the Iran war and threatened a crucial shipping alternative to the Strait of Hormuz. The Houthis' military spokesperson, Brig. Gen. Yahya Saree, said on social media that the rebels launched ballistic missiles and drones in the attacks targeting King Khalid International Airport in the capital, Riyadh, but didn't provide evidence. Flights to and from the airport were briefly disrupted, according to Flightradar24, a tracking platform. Saree said Abha airport, a frequent target of Houthi drones and missiles, was targeted. The rebels also claimed to have hit an air base in the city of Khamis Mushait and two military bases in Najran and Asir. All are in southwestern Saudi Arabia and near the border with Yemen. The spokesperson for the Saudi-led coalition fighting the Houthis, Maj. Gen. Turki al-Malki, said they intercepted and destroyed a ballistic missile north of Riyadh. Saudi Arabia and allied Yemeni forces in recent days have launched a major ground and air offensive against the Houthis in an attempt to retake territory that the rebels seized about a month ago along Yemen's western Red Sea coast and on the Bab el-Mandeb Strait. Those positions gave the rebels better surveillance of shipping as they pursue a blockade of Saudi vessels. On Monday, officials said forces of the Saudi-led coalition fighting in Yemen recaptured several key areas around the strait. The fighting has since then centred in and around the crucial town of Dhubab, some 54 kilometres (33.5 miles) south of the port city of Mokha, according to both the Houthis and the Yemeni government. Clashes were also reported in the district of Waziayah in southwestern Taiz province, which links Yemen's mountainous highlands to the Red Sea, and overlooks roads to the Bab el-Mandeb Strait. Houthis target the airport in Aden with missiles The Houthis also said they launched a missile strike early Wednesday against Yemen's port city of Aden, the seat of the internationally recognised government. An Associated Press journalist heard explosions around 2 am. The rebels hit a military camp close to the Aden airport with ballistic missiles, Saree said. Security authorities in Aden said the Houthis targeted the airport with two missiles, with no casualties. The airport is close to the seat of government. “The targeting of this vital civilian facility represents a direct threat to the safety of civilians, passengers, employees and flight crews,” the Aden police said in a statement. The attack on the Aden airport threatened “a humanitarian disaster,” as one missile hit close to the runway just before the scheduled landing of a flight from Cairo, the Human Rights Ministry said. Flight 603, operated by Yemen's flagship airline, landed safely in Aden at 3:30 am, according to flight tracking platform FlightAware. The ministry said the missile hit as other passengers were waiting to board their flight to the Saudi coastal city of Jeddah. “The Houthis believe that they can maximise Saudi economic costs and compel Saudi Arabia to surrender to Houthi demands by striking civilian infrastructure, such as oil facilities and airports,” the Institute for the Study of War, a Washington-based think tank, wrote in an analysis.

stories.headline: Markets tumble after RBI rate hike; Sensex falls 429 points
stories.title: Markets tumble after RBI rate hike; Sensex falls 429 points
stories.summary: Mumbai, Oct 7 : Equity benchmark indices ended lower on Wednesday, snapping a two-session winning streak after the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) raised the repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.5 per cent and shifted its monetary policy stance to "calibrated tightening", dampening investor sentiment. The Sensex declined 429.11 points, or 0.59 per cent, to close at 72,638.70, while the Nifty fell 173.05 points, or 0.76 per cent, to settle at 22,603.05. Commenting on Nifty technical outlook, experts said that the Nifty fell below 22,700 and closed near the important 22,600 support. "A sustained break below this level could reopen downside toward 22,400, while 22,800 is now the first recovery hurdle," market watchers stated. Investors remained cautious following the central bank's move, which signalled a tighter interest rate environment going forward. Among the Nifty constituents, Titan Company, BEL and Hindalco Industries emerged as the top laggards, weighing on the benchmark indices. Selling pressure was particularly visible in metal stocks, dragging the broader market lower. In the broader market segment, the Nifty MidCap 100 index slipped 0.63 per cent, reflecting weakness in mid-sized stocks. However, the Nifty SmallCap 100 index bucked the trend and gained 0.30 per cent. Sectorally, the Nifty Metal index was the worst performer of the day as investors pared exposure to metal counters. In contrast, the Nifty PSU Bank index outperformed other sectoral gauges and ended with gains, providing some support to the market. Experts said that market participants are likely to closely monitor the impact of the RBI's policy measures on economic growth, liquidity conditions and corporate earnings in the coming months as the central bank focuses on containing inflationary pressures. "Looking ahead, the market focus will turn to the September-quarter earnings season for further direction. A resilient macroeconomic backdrop supports headline expectations, but investors will watch management commentary closely for evidence on whether the companies can absorb rising input costs, retain pricing power and sustain demand through the second half of the fiscal year," analysts stated. --IANS

stories.title: SBI Research expects 6% repo rate: Why inflation is forcing RBI’s hand
stories.summary: In its latest Ecowrap, SBI Research said India’s inflation trajectory could worsen in the coming months, with CPI inflation estimated to peak at around 6.8% in November 2026.

article_sentences: The projection comes after the Monetary Policy Committee unanimously raised the repo rate by 25 bps to 5.50% on October 7, its first rate increase in about four years.
RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra on Wednesday announced a 25-basis-point increase in the policy repo rate to 5.50%, with the MPC unanimously voting in favour of the hike.
The MPC, which met from October 5 to 7, also shifted its policy stance from neutral to calibrated tightening, with the decision supported by a 4-2 majority.
SBI Research said the latest policy marks a significant change in the RBI’s approach.
The central bank’s options in the near term have effectively narrowed to a rate hike or a pause, with rate cuts no longer on the table under current conditions.
The RBI has already raised its FY27 CPI inflation forecast by 20 bps to 5.2%, while its core inflation projection has been increased by 10 bps to 4.4%.
The central bank expects inflation at 4.9% in the second quarter, 6% in the third quarter and 5.7% in the fourth quarter of FY27.
SBI Research believes the worsening inflation trajectory could require a more forceful response.
Its historical analysis shows that the RBI’s peak policy rate has generally been calibrated to the intensity and persistence of inflationary pressures.
With inflation potentially reaching 6.8% in November, SBI estimates that a 6% peak repo rate would be consistent with the historical relationship.

article_sentences: Indians may have to pay more for car, home and personal loans after the federal bank raised its benchmark interest rate for the first time in nearly four years in a bid to rein in inflation.

The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) announced a 25 basis points increase in its repo rate to 5.5% - this is the rate at which it lends money to commercial banks which then pass on the additional cost to customers.
Federal banks across the world have adopted tighter monetary policy amid energy-driven inflation as the war in the Middle East continues.
India's benchmark equity indices Sensex and Nifty fell with investors weighing the implications of higher borrowing costs for consumption and corporate investment.
In his post-policy address, RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra said the decision reflected challenging geopolitical developments, even as the Indian economy remained strong.
He said cuts were "off the table for now", with the central bank likely to either raise rates further or keep them unchanged to contain inflation.

The RBI projects Consumer Price Index (CPI) inflation at 5.2% for 2026-27 - higher than the 5% estimated earlier - to account for price pressure due to weather disruptions, weak monsoon and high volatility in international oil prices.
Crude oil prices are hovering above $100 (£75.33) a barrel resulting in India having to pay even more as the rupee has fallen close to its all-time lows against the dollar.
The country imports around 90% of its crude oil and 50% of its gas needs.
The RBI last raised rates in February 2023, marking the end of its post-pandemic tightening cycle.
During most of 2025, it cut rates to support economic growth before keeping policy unchanged from December 2025 until today's increase.

The rate increase is in line with expectations of economists who say that rising inflation makes a compelling case for it, especially since the economy has displayed enough resilience to absorb its impact without hurting growth.

article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Wednesday upheld the interim bail granted to Congress candidate Milan Pradhan, who is contesting the Nandigram Assembly by-election, observing that the purpose of the relief was to enable him to contest the election and participate in the counting of votes.
Pradhan was arrested on 18th September, 2026 in criminal cases dating back 19 years arising from the 2007 Nandigram agitation.

A bench of Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justice V Mohana dismissed the West Bengal government's plea challenging the High Court's September 29 order granting Pradhan interim bail till October 21.
Voting for the by-election took place on October 6, while counting is scheduled for October 9.

The Court noted that although the cases registered against Pradhan include allegations of serious offences, the High Court's order was primarily intended to ensure that he was not denied an opportunity to contest the election.
The Court thus held that there was no need to interfere with the interim bail, which is operative till October 20, with Pradhan directed to surrender on October 21.
The State, however, will be entitled to raise all its contentions if Pradhan subsequently seeks an extension of interim bail or regular bail, the Court clarified.
“In such circumstances, we do not deem it necessary to interfere with the impugned order.

However, in case the respondent applies for extension of interim bail or seeks enlargement on regular bail, all the contentions raised before us shall be available to the State and shall be considered by the High Court in accordance with law,” the Court ordered.
The Court also made clear that it had not expressed any opinion on the merits of the case.
During the hearing, Solicitor General Tushar Mehta sought to address the concern that Pradhan may have been arrested only because he was contesting the election.

article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Tuesday strongly criticised the Union government for failing to comply with its earlier directions to reconsider welfare measures for officer cadets boarded out of military training due to injuries or disabilities.
A bench of Justice BV Nagarathna, Justice R Mahadevan and Justice DK Upadhyaya was hearing the suo motu case concerning the plight of such cadets.

The Court expressed sharp dissatisfaction over the Centre's affidavit, noting that there had been no genuine reconsideration of the recommendations of the 2015 Sabharwal Committee report despite clear directions issued on August 4, 2026.
“What is this scant attitude you are showing to the court?
You say we disposed it of in 2022 and there ends the matter.
What is the attitude on the part of the department?” Justice Nagarathna observed during the hearing.

The bench pointed out that the Centre's affidavit merely referred to meetings held in 2022 and extracted earlier decisions rejecting disability pension and ex-servicemen (ESM) status for outboarded officer cadets.
There was “no whisper” that the Sabharwal Committee recommendations had been reconsidered in light of the court's intervention, the judges said.
Justice Mahadevan noted that one of the key recommendations relating to disability pension had not been revisited after the August 4 order.
“Pursuant to our 4th August direction, there is no reconsideration,” he said.

The Court observed that ordinary recruits who are boarded out receive disability pension and other benefits, while officer cadets - whose numbers are relatively small (around 400 over many years, or roughly 40 per year) - are denied similar treatment.
Amicus Curiae Senior Advocate Rekha Palli highlighted this disparity and submitted that the cadets were seeking parity.

stories.headline: Special NIA court rejects bail plea of separatist leader Shabir Shah in 1996 violence case
stories.title: Special NIA court rejects bail plea of separatist leader Shabir Shah in 1996 violence case
stories.summary: Jammu, Oct 7: A special NIA court here has rejected the bail application of separatist leader Shabir Ahmad Shah in connection with a case arising from a 1996 FIR relating to violence, stone-pelting and firing on police personnel during a funeral procession in Srinagar. While rejecting the bail plea, Special Judge Prem Sagar held that the application "needs no consideration at this stage", observing that there was a "well-founded apprehension" that if released, Shah was likely to continue such activities to the detriment of national security and public order. Shah (73) was arrested in April by the National Investigation Agency (NIA) in connection with the three-decade-old terror case related to mob violence and firing on policemen during a militant's funeral at Naaz crossing in Srinagar. His arrest came shortly after he was released on bail after nearly seven years of imprisonment in other NIA cases including one related to terror funding. Hearing the bail plea on Tuesday, the NIA court said it has already declared four persons as protected witnesses in the case and charges are yet to be framed against the accused. "Court is conscious of the fact that the only offence under the UAPA that is invoked against the applicant/accused is Section 13 only, which falls within Chapter III of the Act which does not attract the rigours of its Section 43-D(5) and the embargo on bail contained in Section 43-D(5) applies, by its express terms, only to offences 'punishable under Chapters IV and VI' of the Act but every case under UAPA has serious consequences and to be examined viz a viz nature of allegations, centrality of the role, protected witnesses, risk of intimidation, possibility of reactivation of networks etc," the judge said in his 23-page order. The order said any enlargement of the applicant on bail at this stage carries a reasonable apprehension of prejudice to the fair conduct of the trial and may adversely affect the confidence and security of the protected witnesses. On the plea of parity, the court ruled that Shah could not claim bail merely because some co-accused had been released. It distinguished their cases, noting that they had been granted bail after the investigation concerning them was over and the investigating officer no longer required their custody. The NIA had opposed the bail, arguing that Shah was allegedly a "principal leader of the procession", with the prosecution attributing to him an active role in allegedly raising provocative slogans and delivering inflammatory speeches before violence erupted. The agency also cited the presence of protected witnesses and apprehension of their intimidation. The NIA took over the investigation of the 1996 case in April on the directions of the Ministry of Home Affairs and subsequently filed a charge sheet before the NIA Special Court in Jammu on July 10. Shah along with other separatist leaders including Shakeel Ahmad Bakshi and Javid Ahmad Mir have been named in the charge sheet as accused in the case. Separatist leaders Syed Ali Shah Geelani, Abdul Gani Lone and Mohammad Yaqoob Wakeel were also named as accused, but proceedings against them abated following their death. Shah's counsel argued that the sole basis for rejection of his earlier bail plea as "premature" had ceased to exist, as the NIA had subsequently filed its charge sheet on July 10, and the investigation qua the applicant stood concluded. Counsel submitted that the earlier bail plea had not been rejected on merits and that, with the chargesheet now on record, there was no impediment to considering the plea on its merits. The defence also questioned the prosecution case, arguing that there was no allegation that Shah carried or used a weapon or fired any shot, with the firing attributed to unidentified armed persons. The defence also relied on Shah's prolonged incarceration, advanced age and the Supreme Court's March order granting him bail in another NIA case, arguing that continued detention would offend his right to speedy trial under Article 21.

stories.headline: SC expresses displeasure over Rajpal Yadav’s conduct in cheque cases
stories.title: SC expresses displeasure over Rajpal Yadav’s conduct in cheque cases
stories.summary: New Delhi, Oct 7 : The Supreme Court on Wednesday directed actor and comedian Rajpal Yadav to deposit Rs 1.15 crore with the apex court registry after his counsel submitted that the amount was ready to be deposited immediately, while another Rs 85 lakh would be arranged through a prospective buyer of his ancestral property, as part of arrangements to pay Rs 2 crore in connection with multiple cheque dishonour cases. A Bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana was hearing Yadav and his wife Radha Yadav's pleas challenging the Delhi High Court judgment upholding their conviction in seven cheque dishonour cases under the Negotiable Instruments Act. During the hearing, the CJI Kant-led Bench was informed that Yadav had arranged Rs 1.15 crore through demand drafts, while a prospective buyer of his ancestral property, who was present in court, was willing to pay another Rs 85 lakh as an advance. Yadav’s counsel told the top court that the buyer was not presently willing to register the sale documents due to Pitru Paksha and wanted to proceed with the registration after the commencement of Navratri. The counsel further submitted that the buyer was willing to deposit the Rs 85 lakh by way of a demand draft on Monday. However, the Supreme Court questioned the overall value of the transaction, remarking that the liability was substantially higher than Rs 2 crore. "What will be the total sale consideration? Because the liability is much more than Rs 2 crore," the CJI Kant-led Bench asked. The counsel said the property was valued at more than Rs 30 crore and confirmed that the prospective buyer had the capacity to make the proposed payment. The complainant's counsel agreed to the proposal and submitted that if Rs 2 crore was paid immediately, Yadav could be granted additional time to pay the remaining amount. The CJI Kant-led Bench suggested that Rs 1.15 crore be deposited immediately, with the remaining Rs 85 lakh to be transferred on Monday, after which the top court would lay down a schedule for payment of the balance amount. During the hearing, the Supreme Court expressed displeasure over Yadav’s conduct in complying with its earlier directions and indicated that it was inclined to enhance his three-month imprisonment sentence to two years. Justice Bagchi observed that the apex court was not satisfied with Yadav’s conduct and said the accommodation being extended to him was aimed at ensuring that the complainant recovered the money. The top court’s latest order came after it had, on October 5, found that its September 15 direction had not been complied with. On that occasion, the CJI Kant-led Bench had observed that a photocopy of a purported Rs 50 lakh demand draft was produced with a claim that the draft would reach Delhi the following day. The Supreme Court had then granted a final opportunity to Yadav to pay a total of Rs 2 crore and posted the matter for October 7. On September 15, the apex court had granted Yadav two weeks as a last opportunity to deposit at least Rs 2 crore, after recording that its earlier direction to deposit Rs 5 crore had not been complied with. The Supreme Court is hearing Yadav and his wife Radha Rajpal Yadav’s petitions challenging the Delhi High Court judgment upholding their conviction in seven cheque dishonour cases under the Negotiable Instruments Act. The Delhi High Court had on July 10 upheld Yadav’s conviction while reducing his sentence from six months to three months’ simple imprisonment in each of the seven cases. It had also reduced the fine from Rs 1.60 crore to Rs 1.05 crore in each case, with the substantive sentences directed to run concurrently. The High Court had taken into account payments already made by Yadav to the complainant, M/s Murli Projects Pvt Ltd., during the pendency of the proceedings. Yadav and his wife have challenged the judgment before the Supreme Court, contending that a subsequent consent agreement between the parties was not properly considered by the courts below. The petitioners have relied on the Supreme Court’s judgment in M/s Gimpex Private Limited vs Manoj Goel, arguing that the subsequent agreement between the parties ought to have brought an end to the original complaint proceedings. --IANS

article_sentences: Coal inventories at India’s power stations are close to a five-year low, with plants equivalent to more than 40 per cent of the nation’s coal-fired capacity left with just four days of reserves or even less, a level that raises the risk of widespread blackouts.

Unusually warm temperatures and erratic rains have kept demand for cooling, irrigation and industry strong through the day well into October, a month when the weather should typically begin to cool across the subcontinent.
The supply of coal, meanwhile, has been disrupted by heavy downpours that stopped work at some mines, and by continued bottlenecks in rail capacity — forcing plants to dip into inventories.
As of October 4, some 69 power stations — more than two-fifths of the nation’s coal power fleet — had fuel for just four days or less, a level monitored as a minimum by plant operators.
That’s the lowest since December 2021, during a post-pandemic energy crisis that hit India and other major consumers in the region, as the return of industries ran down depleted stockpiles.

India has seen breakneck solar and wind growth over the past decades, but coal still produces nearly 70 per cent of electricity in the country, leaving the power system vulnerable to weather events, disruptions in transport or strikes at mines.
Almost 90 per cent of plants with low inventories are located away from coal mines.
The disruption could have effects lasting into next summer, as the months through February, usually the coolest period in the country, offer a narrow window to rebuild inventories.
Any interruption could hamper power plants’ efforts to prepare for heatwaves or unexpected spikes in demand.

“As the weather cools down over the next few months, it would give some breathing room to the system, allowing distribution utilities to carry out some daily load shedding to reduce demand,” said Rupesh Sankhe, senior vice president for research at Elara Capital India Pvt.
“Meanwhile, Coal India and railways will need to ensure supplies to power stations pick up so that we are well prepared for the summer.”

article_sentences: "One blinks, others follow within days." That is Equirus Securities' summarization of past tariff hikes taken by telecom operators over the last decade.
Equirus highlighted this while initiating coverage on the telecom companies back on September 28.
This assumes greater significance now that Bharti Airtel has gone ahead and increased its postpaid tariff plans by ₹50 across the board.
Postpaid currently contributes between 8% to 12% of Bharti Airtel's topline, according to industry estimates.
The key question now comes to mind is, with Bharti having made the move, will both Jio and Vodafone Idea follow suit?
Equirus analyses these past patterns.

Calling it a move to "survive" and not "grow", Equirus highlighted how Bharti Airtel and Vodafone Idea rolled out their precise plan details on December 1, 2019, and implementing those from December 3.
Three days later, Reliance Jio implemented its "All-in-One" plan.
Tariffs were raised between 20% to 40% and operators reworked their 28-day, 84-day and 365-day plans.
As a result of this tariff hike, Bharti Airtel's Average Revenue Per User (ARPU) jumped from ₹135 in the third quarter of financial year 2020 to ₹166 in the third quarter of financial year 2021.
Reliance Jio saw a similar jump from ₹128 to ₹151, while Vodafone Idea's ARPU increased from ₹109 to ₹121 during the same timeframe.
Two years later, in November 2021, Bharti Airtel once again took the lead in announcing a 20% to 25% blanket increase across all prepaid plans, which took effect from November 26 that year.

Tariffs were raised between 20% to 40% and operators reworked their 28-day, 84-day and 365-day plans.
As a result of this tariff hike, Bharti Airtel's Average Revenue Per User (ARPU) jumped from ₹135 in the third quarter of financial year 2020 to ₹166 in the third quarter of financial year 2021.
